Since the start of the ceasefire until today, COGAT has coordinated the entry of more than 2 million tons of food into the Gaza Strip since the start of the ceasefire in October 2025. This humanitarian aid, coordinated with the UN, international organizations, and donor countries, consists of varied, nutritious food to meet the nutritional needs of the Gazan civilian population. The deliveries support markets, bakeries, community kitchens, and other food distribution facilities. The large-scale entry of food has also contributed to a significant decline in prices and improved access to essential goods for civilians across Gaza. The achievement of this level of aid demonstrates Israel’s commitment to coordinating humanitarian assistance. COGAT continues to monitor the humanitarian situation in Gaza, together with its partners on the ground, and will continue its efforts to ensure that essential supplies reach the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.

COGAT continues to maintain close coordination with international actors to monitor the chickenpox situation in the Gaza Strip. A continuous assessment of the situation is being conducted by the relevant international organizations, alongside ongoing joint monitoring and coordination between COGAT and humanitarian partners. At this stage, the United Nations does not intend to conduct a dedicated vaccination campaign against chickenpox, as the disease is generally not considered life-threatening, and vaccination campaigns are not typically used as the primary response measure for such cases. At the same time, COGAT continues to work closely with the UN and additional humanitarian organizations to strengthen water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) components throughout the Gaza Strip — efforts that play an important role in reducing health risks and supporting the prevention of disease transmission. COGAT continues to work with all relevant humanitarian actors to support an appropriate response to the situation. Should additional requests be submitted for the entry of medical supplies or other necessary equipment related to this matter, COGAT will be prepared to review such requests and work with relevant partners to identify practical solutions.

Abu Dhabi Police claimed first place in the Men’s White and Blue Belt category, followed by Dubai Police in second and Sharjah Police in third. Abu Dhabi Police also secured first place in both the Men’s and Women’s Open Weight divisions, while Dubai Police finished second and the Ministry of Interior team placed third in both categories.
